title: Length of Last Word
scenario:
You get a string s of words and spaces. Return the length of the last word — the last run of non-space characters. There's always at least one word.

Example 1:
Input: s = "Hello World"
Output: 5

Example 2:
Input: s = "   fly me   to   the moon  "
Output: 4
Why: the last word is "moon" — the spaces after it don't count.

Example 3:
Input: s = "luffy is still joyboy"
Output: 6

Constraints:
1 <= len(s) <= 10000
s holds only English letters and spaces, with at least one word.

Write: def length_of_last_word(s) — the driver calls it on s = "Hello World" and prints the length.

idea.rule: Spaces can trail the last word — split into words first, then measure the last one.
idea.detail: Like problem 007 (Name tags), split() is the tool: with no argument it breaks on any run of spaces and throws empty pieces away, so leading, doubled and trailing spaces all vanish. Measuring from the last space instead (like problem 026's slicing) works only when nothing comes after the last word — one trailing space and the 'word' you measure is empty.

model_restatement: Return the length of the last word in the string, ignoring any spaces around it.

clarify.question: Can there be spaces after the last word?
clarify.answer: Yes — any number. They don't count.

clarify.question: What if the string is a single word?
clarify.answer: Then that word is the last word.

clarify.question: Can the string be only spaces?
clarify.answer: No — there's always at least one word.

clarify_fallback: Good question — assume the simple case.
blueprint: Find the last space; the last word is everything after it, so its length is len(s) minus that position minus 1.
draft_code:
def length_of_last_word(s):
    last_space = s.rfind(" ")
    return len(s) - last_space - 1

print(length_of_last_word(s))

why_line: Measuring from the last space works on "Hello World" — the last space is right before "World". But in "a " the last space is the trailing one, so the draft measures what comes after it: nothing — 0.

explain.rule: Measuring from the last space is reading the last word off a sign by finding its last gap — a stray gap after the word leaves you reading empty board.
explain.bridge: last_space is 5, the gap before "World". Where would the last space be in "a " — and what comes after it?

fix.rule: Split on whitespace — it drops empty pieces — and take the length of the last word.

walk.gloss: Break on any run of spaces; empty pieces disappear.

alternatives.note: Walk back from the end: skip trailing spaces, then count characters until the next space — no list needed.
